title: Isomerism in benzene
textbookText: Figure 15. 4 Orbital Structure of benzene For detail watch the video in the link: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EgQAOSRfz3E Isomerism in benzene The organic compounds having the same molecular formula but of different structure are called isomers. The property shown by the compound is called isomerism. 1. Monosubstituted isomers of benzene: all six carbon atoms of benzene are equivalent.
So, replacement of any of six hydrogen atoms gives only one mono-substituted benzene.
2. Disubstituted isomers of benzene: There are three positional isomers of benzene.

3. Tri-substituted isomers of benzene: Number of isomers depends on the nature of substituents. If all three substituents are the same, three isomers are possible. They are vicinal, asymmetrical and symmetrical.

a. By decarboxylation of sodium benzoate: When sodium benzoate is heated with soda-lime (NaOH+CaO) benzene is obtained by removing –COONa. In this reaction, one carbon atom is lost from the substrate reagent. So, it is called a decarboxylation reaction. Rxn:
Requirements: Sod. Benzoate Soda-lime heat

b. By heating phenol with zinc dust Activity: 4 Take about 5 ml of phenol in a test tube. Add a piece of zinc in it. Heat the mixture. After sometime you will see pale yellow liquid with pleasant gasoline like petroleum odour i.e. benzene. Requirements: Phenol Zincdust heat

c. By aromatization or polymerization of ethyne
When three molecules of ethyne or acetylene are passed into iron tube or cu-tube, at
about 5000C, under pressure of about 25 atm, benzene is obtained by polymerization.
Aliphatic compounds are cyclized. So, this reaction is also known as cyclization or
aromatization reaction.

Physical Properties of Benzene
1. Benzene is a colorless, aromatic odour and volatile liquid.
2. Benzene is immiscible in water but soluble in organic solvents.
3. Boiling point of benzene is 80.090C i.e. ~ 80.10C and melting point is 5.530C.
4. It has a density of 0.87g cm-3.
